description: City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council (CBMDC) and Leeds City Council (LCC) wishes to continue the success of the Northern MAX accelerator programme by launching the Northern MAX Accelerator in early 2024.  Northern MAX Accelerators are an intensive business support programme delivered in Bradford and Leeds to serve and support the economic recovery of digital technology businesses that are under three years old and based in the CBMDC and LCC authority areas.  As such, CBMDC and LCC are inviting submissions from Service Providers to deliver an accelerator programme with a digital technology sector focus to a fifth cohort in Bradford and Leeds.  The Northern MAX Accelerator, funded by CBMDC and LCC (through the UK Shared prosperity fund, as part of the Leeds Hyper-Local Programme allocation) will deliver a programme of activity to enhance the competitiveness of small and  medium sized enterprises until June 2024.   The Northern MAX Accelerator will be aligned to the AD:VENTURE programme. CBMDC is a partner in the LCC led AD:VENTURE programme; alongside the West Yorkshire Combined Authority, the four other local authorities in West Yorkshire, the Business Enterprise Fund and The Prince's Trust. The AD:VENTURE programme targets start-ups and businesses that have been trading up to three years and identified as having growth potential (aspiring to attain the VAT threshold of a turnover of £85,000 within two years; with the propensity to create jobs; trading predominantly business to business and is available to most business sectors. AD:VENTURE will also support business to consumer applicants if it is likely that 50% of its turnover will be derived from customers outside of West Yorkshire. The package of support includes; one to one support from an AD:VENTURE Business Manager; workshops and webinars to upskill entrepreneurs, owners and managers; potential access to a loan fund and a  grant scheme; and events to promote peer to peer learning.

title: Play Streets Enablement Grant (Kidz Klub)
description: Play Streets have been established in Leeds since 2015, with around 100 active applications in place by 2019. In 2018, Leeds won a national Play award in recognition of its support for Play Streets. The Covid-19 pandemic disrupted the success of Play Streets in Leeds. In addition, it was evident by 2021 that few active applications were made from areas in the 10% most deprived neighbourhoods in the UK. The benefits of Play Streets were identified as likely to be greater in these areas, especially in terms of mitigating the impact of the pandemic, when access to green space and spaces to play and be active was identified as a significant issue for families living in poverty, in comparison to more affluent families. Concomitantly, the need for support to enable Play Streets to be developed in areas experiencing deprivation was seen as likely to be greater. As a result, a Play Streets Enablement project was launched in 2021. Since then, at least 25 Play Streets have been established in the 10% most deprived areas, when there were none prior to 2021. Many of these Play Streets are organised on a regular basis. The project has received external funding from the Holiday Activities Fund (HAF/Healthy Holidays) and also from the Better Care Fund. Two models of support have been trialled, and processes have been evaluated as the model has developed. Local partnerships are now well established, and awareness of Play Streets is growing in communities facing multiple challenges.

title: Play Streets Enablement Grant (Incredible Edible)
description: Play Streets have been established in Leeds since 2015, with around 100 active applications in place by 2019. In 2018, Leeds won a national Play award in recognition of its support for Play Streets. The Covid-19 pandemic disrupted the success of Play Streets in Leeds. In addition, it was evident by 2021 that few active applications were made from areas in the 10% most deprived neighbourhoods in the UK. The benefits of Play Streets were identified as likely to be greater in these areas, especially in terms of mitigating the impact of the pandemic, when access to green space and spaces to play and be active was identified as a significant issue for families living in poverty, in comparison to more affluent families. Concomitantly, the need for support to enable Play Streets to be developed in areas experiencing deprivation was seen as likely to be greater. As a result, a Play Streets Enablement project was launched in 2021. Since then, at least 25 Play Streets have been established in the 10% most deprived areas, when there were none prior to 2021. Many of these Play Streets are organised on a regular basis. The project has received external funding from the Holiday Activities Fund (HAF/Healthy Holidays) and also from the Better Care Fund. Two models of support have been trialled, and processes have been evaluated as the model has developed. Local partnerships are now well established, and awareness of Play Streets is growing in communities facing multiple challenges.

title: NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (Leeds Place) AQP Minor Surgery Services
description:
NHS West Yorkshire Integrated Care Board (WY ICB) has accredited bidders to provide the AQP Minor Surgery Services.

The service will be delivered to Leeds patients only and not across West Yorkshire.

The aims of the service are to provide a minor surgery service that will:
- Ensure equitable, timely, high quality and appropriate access
- Ensure patients are seen and treated in a safe environment, appropriate to their care needs
- Provide a streamlined patient referral process

The minor surgery service is commissioned to achieve three key goals:
- Ensuring equality of access so that Leeds patients who are registered with general practices who do not participate in the minor surgery DES, still have access to those services through referral to a community minor surgery provider of their choice
- Ensuring that lower complexity minor surgery cases can be managed through referral to a community minor surgery provider of their choice, rather than to a hospital service
- Enable other community services to access treatments that would otherwise be delivered by a hospital provider.

title: Online Reading List System and Digital Content Solution
description:
Leeds Trinity University (LTU) is seeking bids from suppliers who are able to provide online reading list systems and digital content solutions. 

Currently LTU has approximately 9,500 FTE students, of whom 4,100 are studying at Leeds Trinity University itself, and 5,400 on LTU franchised programmes at partner institutions, and 207 FTE academic staff.   

There are currently 1735 modules managed directly by LTU and 407 modules managed by partners with 658 (LTU) and 143 (partners) reading lists hosted in the current system. 

The University is however in a period of growth with new teaching programmes coming online over the next few years.  In addition to this the University is opening a new City Centre Campus at 1 Trevelyan Square in September 2024, so all solutions offered need to be scalable to meet current and future demands. 

The tender is intended to result in a contract with a single supplier, although the University reserves the right to not award or award to multiple suppliers where it is considered that this offers best value for money.  The contract period is 5+1+1.
